tips.comment: Jasmine Dairy is going the right way and ran a cracker when just touched off at Ffos Las last time. She’s got race fitness on her side, drops in grade, and with support coming in again, she looks like the one to beat.

The model I run simulates this race and suggests Lady Kluck can win this one. Second highest RPR of the field, and wears a hood for the first time with Harry Skelton on board. Open to more improvement. Jasmin d'Airy likely the main competition here as Ben Sutton is on board claiming 3 lbs.

Ran a perfectly good race when 4th at Newbury in a Class 2 handicap and could have been more involved in the finish if put into the race earlier. Class 4 today, and with a sharper track like Plumpton, should play to his strengths.
His last win was at this course, and his mark is untouched from that victory after two placings since then, sliding him down slightly.
He is the pace angle in this contest and should go well for a long way. James Bowen is always good on these types of horses.

In a very tough-looking race, I'm going to take a risk on Jolyjump. This gelding will be wearing first-time cheekpieces, which could spark a little more improvement, and also the good ground could work in his favor. The yard does very well here. Caoilin Quinn in the saddle again. 10st 8lbs on this gelding's back, that's the lowest I can see that he's saddled as far back as late 2023. Hopefully, he can go well.
Second at Ffos Las two weeks ago and kept on going despite hitting a fence too hard. Can go well on soft to good going and is an each-way claimant in this.
He slides down for an 8L defeat last time and should do a lot better now with that, plus some cheekpieces being added for a bigger target.

My Friend Sean got the job done nicely at Chepstow when well backed and looked to have a bit in hand despite idling late on. This is a tougher race and he’s up in the weights, but with that bit of improvement to come, he’s still one to take seriously.

On the negative side, Harry Derham's mare is having her first hurdling experience in mixed company, but I firmly believe the unexposed 5-year-old is the one to be on. Winner of a weak maiden here in November, she has then had to run in a couple of warm novices carrying a penalty, culminating in the 100k Kelso mares race, her first handicap, last month. On goes the tongue tie, and with a big drop in grade allied to a decent surface, I think a big run is on the cards.

Jorebel is a 6-year-old gelding trained by Chris Gordon. He has only contested two handicaps and ran well for a long way in the latest at Uttoxeter. He runs today off bottom weight of 10st 9lb and 10st 6lb with the useful Freddie Gordon's 3lb conditional claim. Chris Gordon's stable comes to Plumpton in good form, having won with his last two runners, Highway One O Five at 11-2 and King William Rufus. Chris Gordon plunders races at Plumpton, winning 103 races, more wins than at any other track, and it could be a fruitful day following Chris Gordon's four entries. Out of a once-raced dam related to three others who all won, notably Fact To File who has recorded an RPR of 177, thus Jorebel is definitely one to consider today off a lowly mark of 86.
It's likely that he just ran into one last time, and in that context, it was still a big effort. Only gone up 1 lb, so basically getting in the same.

Unanswered Prayers is a 9-year-old gelding trained by Chris Gordon, a yard in good form, winning with their last two runners. Unanswered Prayers is 5/28 wins and a two-time chase winner in class 3 handicap chases off marks of 126 (Tom Cannon) and 121 (Freddie Gordon and a 5lb claim). He runs off 125 today, so looks well treated and has no problems with today's trip, having won over 27f and is a two-time winner on today's good ground. Chris Gordon also targets this track, having landed 103 winners, the biggest tally of wins than any other track. Unanswered Prayers, who is also a course winner over hurdles, is definitely one for the shortlist.

An intriguing two days of racing at Plumpton ahead for the Mullins-Skelton trainer title showdown. Hidden Heroics is one of two Dan Skelton trained runners in this 3m1f handicap chase (Class 3). Has won four of 16 chase starts all at 3 miles and is one of the more experienced jumpers in the race. Wins over fences from marks between 120 and 129 so capable off OR126. Unreliable type, badly out of form in only two starts this season but they were at an inadequate 2m4f. Can get involved today back at a more suitable trip.

3rd in the County Hurdle at the Cheltenham Festival is the best recent form on offer here, and ABSURDE should take all the beating with trainer Willie Mullins looking for big prize money to take the Trainers' Championship.

Our Champ is a 7-year-old gelding trained by Chris Gordon, a yard in good form, winning with their last two entrants. Plumpton is a track that the yard targets, landing 103 wins at Plumpton. Our Champ is a four-time winner under rules, and all wins have come on today's good ground, two of which have come over today's course and distance, including a win in this race last year off a 13lb lower mark. He has since won at Ascot off 131, beating Break My Soul (122), who is now rated 140, and Secret Squirrel (126), who has won since and is rated some 6lb higher. Our Champ is more than capable of landing this contest for a second consecutive year with conditions being optimal.

Daddy Long Legs was in my tracker from the hurdle race at Cheltenham and only showed up for a race at Punchestown later, so it must have been a late entry for this. Three other Mullins runners, but I like the booking of Nico de Boinville here. However, it needs to be more handy on this tight track.

Handicapper has given him a chance here, dropping him down to a mark of 139 and dropping back in distance. He's just 1 lb above his last winning mark. He won the Gerry Feilden on that occasion, finding plenty to fend off Bad by 3/4L, giving him 15 lbs in weight also. He's run well on occasions this season, particularly his close-up 3rd in a Grade 2 behind Golden Ace and Burdett Road. That form has been boosted since with the two mentioned occupying the same positions in the Champion Hurdle at the festival. Admittedly, he comes into this with a bit to prove at present following 2 lesser runs. He did win his sole run over CD, however, beating a decent horse in Master Chewy. He gave him 7 lbs in weight and still beat him 2L. That type of form would see him thereabouts if bouncing back to form this time.

The Skeltons remain in contention for the trainers' championship, and Willie Mullins has sent a strong hand to Plumpton to ensure they stay at the top. However, Knickerbockerglory could put a dent in their bid. Often front-runs, and despite pulling up in this race last year, has been kept lightly raced this season and raced with much credit - picking up a win and 2 narrow defeats by less than 2 lengths. Has the top speed rating of the field and might be difficult to reel in if getting into a good jumping rhythm.
The Dan Skelton trained She's a Saint is up nine pounds here but arrives in great form with eight in a row inside the first two home and should go well again here.

The model I run suggests Afadil should win this, but given the huge odds on offer, Each Way seems the smarter play here and gives some margin for error. I don't typically like Each Way betting, but this should still offer value. Afadil steps out with the second highest RPR of the field, by far the lowest weight to carry. Previously had good form before a poor run at Aintree, but if you're willing to overlook that one, this looks like an opportunity.

This is a different ask for She’s A Saint, for all she’s a tempter at the odds to go well. The one that ultimately tempted me was the formerly classy Sir Gerhard stepping into handicap company. He’s flattered to deceive this year, but did finish 3rd in a decent Sandown Grade 2 around this time last year. His latest run has worked out pretty well, with the other 3 of the front 4 running solid races in defeat in decent company since. He could make light of an opening handicap mark of 147, albeit the British handicapper hasn’t given him much rope on this season's form. He’s got some decent efforts to his name on better ground, and I think he has a better chance than his odds at rolling back the years here.
Shakeyatailfeather won last week at Cheltenham without having to break a sweat. Strike whilst the iron's hot and all that, but can follow up here for the double.
The weight could get to him after two straight wins, but he is a front runner on a course that suits and will go well for a long time, if not the whole way.
His last memory here was a wide win where he demolished the competition. This is tougher, but he should be a lot better than last time off a break.
Centara was a decent third on chase debut last month after a short break. I would expect more now, second up and back at 2m3f, which is the distance he had his last two wins at.
Sooner or later, Heros is going to find his form again. He certainly hasn't been pulling up any trees this season. However, his mark is now falling, and today could be the day he starts his comeback.

The model I run suggests Belgarum can win this one ahead of the others. Prior form is nothing special but steps out here fresh for the first time since a wind operation. Joint highest RPR of the field. Previous course and distance winner, so does have the history onside. Each way still offers value at 21s.

Electric Mason is a 6-year-old gelding trained by Chris Gordon, a trainer very much in form, winning with his last two runners and targeting Plumpton, picking up 103 wins. Electric Mason didn't cut much ice on handicap hurdle debut at Cheltenham in the Martin Pipe but has scope for improvement now dropped 2 lb to 130, having opened at 117. He handles today's good ground, and Electric Mason could be capable of a very good day for Chris Gordon, whose four entries hold significant chances.
Mr. Escobar looks like an interesting one here, returning to hurdling from the AW for WM. Looks fairly unexposed and well-handicapped and could win some valuable prize money here.

A good race on a cracking card here tomorrow and a number who I have noted this season run in this race. But as last year's runner-up in the Sussex Champion Hurdle and with the best course form on the card, this lad is where I land. His best days have come on good ground and his first run after a break at Bangor was encouraging with the form working out well. Would hope for a drift to 8s by my tissue but every chance EW.
Getalead had some nice wins in autumn before disappointing last time. Now, coming back after a nice break, the fresh horse could run well.
Makes turf debut. Shaped well the last twice on AW and is fancied now moving up in trip, which should suit.

Fiddlers Green was well-backed to win this race last year and looks set to do the same plot job this year. Back to that winning mark and 7lb claimed by the jockey, showed he's in form with a spin on his unfavored all-weather last time and will be set to go today.
Harlington is consistent at this level, placed over this course and distance, and proven at this trip. Capable of bouncing back after a luckless favorite run.

Third of nine around here 17 days ago and a regular runner here. She has scope for improvement and is off a lowly mark today. She is likely to be ridden closer to the leader today and has a chance with this sort of strategy.

Khangai has won off higher marks in the past and will now race off a lower weight than his last winning mark with Mason Paetel's claim. He's been riding well with a winner midweek and going close with a 40/1 runner on Friday. Likes to go off from the front and could slip the field. Trainer couldn't be in better form

Formal Address put in a respectable performance when finishing fifth out of nine runners in a competitive handicap at Brighton over 9.9 furlongs on good ground just over a week ago (starting at odds of 11/1). Despite not making the frame, the gelding showed decent mid-race pace and kept on steadily in the final furlong, suggesting there’s more to come with the right conditions. I think going up in trip would suit, judging by the finishing speed last time out. I think the value is here with this selection.

Sir Edward Lear had a cracking debut when winning at Ripon on good, and although not so good last time out, that was on soft. I think the return to firmer ground today on handicap debut could see a return to the top step.

I'm going against two in this. I've previously tipped and plumbed for Polling Day, which ran a good race on stable debut, with that race having some substance to it now. This very stiff track looks likely to suit after that not knocked about last run over this trip.
Chicago Storm won before taking a break and returns here off a fairly low weight. If it can go well fresh, it can go close in this one.

Think Of A Name looked smart winning here in the autumn and has been a consistent type overall aside from one quiet run. The quicker ground is a bit of an unknown but the return of a top jockey is a big plus and the trainer and jockey have a strong record in turf handicaps (27 runs, 9 wins, 1.83 A/E, +25pts @ 92% ROI).

Alashos has immediately caught my attention here and for very good reason was last seen at Nottingham 8 day's ago where finishing a respectable 3rd/7 over the 6 furlong trip drops in trip here going over the 5 furlong trip that being a wise move by his connections as this very speedy individual can be very effective over this sprinting distance now racing on very suitable turf track that can greatly suit this speedy individual the blinkers are applied for the first time and they can have a positive effect currently operating on an unchanged mark of 69 James Horton's gelded son of showcasing is likely to put up a very bold showing front running performance and will be hard to get past here at the Bath track given his nature of going jockey A J Farragher takes the ride and can give this his best shot bold showing is anticipated and he is certainly one to consider to take this class 5 handicap

Second horse that the trainer sends to this meeting and has an excellent chance of breaking the maiden tag. Ran here on debut, finishing third. Hasn't been beaten by more than 2 lengths since handicapping. Races off bottom weight and has a 3lb claimer on board.

Looks a big price. Ran a creditable 3rd over this distance last year, less than 1.5 lengths to the leader, and followed up here with a second place. First two outings this year have been poor, but now running 6lb lower than the 2nd place. Trainer and jockey also have a decent record here.

Electric Storm stands out for consistent speed figures and suitability for today’s conditions. With a reliable turn of foot and positive trainer-jockey synergy, she looks primed for success against this field. Previous performances on similar ground and class make her a leading contender.

First Instinct had two good opening runs in Aug/Sept when winning in C5 and C2 at 6f but was a bit duff when last out at 7f in G3. She is worth a chance that the drop to 5f could suit on this return, as we know she can go well when fresh.

A winner over this 5 furlong trip at Meydan in March 2024 and also a winner over 7 furlongs at Chelmsford in 2023. That proven stamina over further could be significant in the uphill finish here as will the drop in trip after racing over 6 furlongs at Doncaster at the end of last month.
Englemere had some decent wins last year, including a listed event carrying 9-2. While I would like to have seen a better draw, I expect more today back with the girls carrying 8-12 EW 3P.

2nd of 9 here by a length last time out. This run may prove important given a number of others are running their first race of the year. Good jockey on board and the trainer has a strong record at this course. Has won at C&D in the past.

Sixteen One has been placed for the last two runs this year, with the latest showing improvement when stepped up to 1 mile and second. She could continue to improve now, second up after a break while still at 1 mile.

Red Admiral was well-supported on seasonal return following a breathing operation. Despite running wide that was his best run so far. He is dropped another grade for handicap debut and should get the mile on fast ground.
Captain Cess made a big improvement when third last August. If he can hit the ground running, this drop to C6 could bring him in the money if getting on with the new trip on this handicap debut.

Red Savitar makes plenty of appeal on paper as a £75,000 Lope Y Fernandez colt with a speedy pedigree and a top jockey booked. The yard has already had a 2yo winner this season and there’s market interest building, so he looks one to take seriously first time out.

An open-looking race where Sunset in Paris appeals at a big-looking 9/1. With question marks over the stamina of a lot of these, including the favourite, the selection looks a sure stayer and wasn't beaten far in a better-looking race at Lingfield last time. He is off the same mark today and should go close.

IRV is too well treated to overlook and he won a race when returning from a similar absence last season. He has won on the all-weather from eleven attempts and the yard and jockey have been among the recent winners. Much of this probably at the very least makes him overpriced given how weak this middle-distance handicap looks.
A previous course winner over a mile here and a runner-up over a mile and a half when last seen at Lingfield at the end of last month. This drop in trip and return to a tapeta surface should suit.

This maiden finally gets the step up in trip that it looks like he's been crying out for. The run for this jockey last time out gave all the clues that he needed further, and he races off 46 here, having started life in handicaps off 65. He's not going to get a better chance than this to get off the mark, and he should be putting in his best work at the end here.

The Ormer Gatherer sprung an 80/1 surprise at Lingfield and needed every yard to do so. Has only had 2 runs (the other over obstacles) for David Bridgewater. This step up in trip should suit based on spells in France and last winning run. Carries less weight now back into handicap, looks good each-way value.

Nebras made a bright start winning at Newmarket and wasn’t out of his depth in the Futurity despite finishing down the field. This is a huge drop in class and with some strong overnight support, he looks very tough to beat if anywhere near ready on his seasonal return.
Adelaide Bay is likely to follow up its most recent win and bring up the double. It looked good for the win, and improvement is likely, carrying less weight than those behind in the market.

Threatening didn’t look the most straightforward last time at Lingfield but showed much more promise on his second start and that form still reads well. He’s had a short break which could help settle him and the yard is in good form, so not one to rule out if things click.

Thanks Dad battled on well to win gamely last time just holding off King Sharjah who reopposes him today. King Sharjah is weighted to reverse the form but with Tom Eaves retaining the ride and partnership there could be a little more improvement to come from my selection who tends to enjoy this venue. Therefore, it is worth sticking with Thanks Dad who looks to be a good each-way play.
A course and distance winner off a mark of 61 in February 2022 and races off 57 here. Excuses last time when running without a hind shoe and the first time visor could sparkle.

Jesse Luc is clearly in a good place right now after winning well at Chelmsford and backing that up with a strong second off a higher mark last time. He’s been well supported in the market on both occasions, which suggests confidence from connections. If he runs to that same level again, he’s got every chance of picking up winning this.

Only raced over course and distance once before, and that was back in February 2024 when sent off favorite off a mark of 70 and runner-up beaten a length and a quarter. Down to a mark of 63 and likely to welcome the drop in trip after racing over 7 furlongs at Newcastle last month when a beaten favorite.

Potentially overlooked in the market for this race. Rated 6lb lower than the last winning mark, and beaten distances suggest he's running better than the form suggests. Also, the form behind a number of horses recently has been boosted by wins or others having top 3 finishes. Speed rating also suggests he has to run to a similar level of late to gain a return from an each-way bet.
Yoshimi won last time out, and although this is a much tougher affair, improvement looks likely and is carrying less weight than others in the race. Each way claims.

One that might outrun its odds in this race is Madame Fenella. She is bred, owned and trained by the family and has slipped down the weights to a mark 7 pounds below her last win. She has a reasonable record around Southwell and carries just 8-7. She might run into a place at long odds.
The Dream Goes On is on a hat-trick here and still has a weight advantage over some of the others in the field. It is expected to bring up the three-timer.
Ninna Collina looks good to get her head in front here after several good runs and has a huge weight advantage compared to the market leader.
Plus Point showed enough promise on its debut run to be in with a decent chance here today if improving on that run to give the OLBG owners a big run for their money today.
The model I run suggests Sharona can win this race. Only 4 years old, looks the progressive type. 11 lbs less to carry than the top of the market with Aaron Anderson on board claiming 3 lbs.

Joining Force comes here off the back of a good second. With improvement likely, it can go one better here. The market leader fell last time out and has potentially knocked some confidence, so the selection can take advantage.

Monty Bodkin tried to make all at Huntingdon last time and was joined by the odds-on favorite with ten lengths back to the third horse when he fell at the last flight. This looks like an easier maiden hurdle to win.
Loch Frisa finished 2nd last time out, finishing behind a good sort. They can go one better here or at least go close. 3 places each way.

Presenting Milan is a 5-year-old gelding trained by Richard Hawker. He is a bumper winner and wasn't disgraced in a listed bumper on his last start. He makes his hurdles debut and is a fourth foal related to three individual winners: Presenting Yeats (trained by today's trainer), who has won seven races, and Mr. Yeats, a five-time winner. The dam Va'vite (IRE) wasn't a slouch, winning 5 out of 20. Presenting Milan has a nice pedigree, which has produced a number of winners, and can make a good fist of things today on his hurdles debut under Harry Reed.

Zucayan has been knocking on the door of late and running on well late, suggesting today's extra couple of furlongs will suit, as will the ground. Was behind Greatness Awaits on penultimate start but weighted to reverse that form today, and many other rivals have a bit to prove. Good value for the win at 3/1 or above.

The model I run suggests Gms Prince can win this one ahead of Zucayan in second and Sambezi in third. Gms Prince has the second highest RPR of the field, but it did not translate to a high OR. This leaves Gms Prince with the lowest weight to carry, with Tabitha Worsley on board taking off another 3 lbs.

Looks like a good each way bet here. With a record of one win and five places from six runs in class 5 hurdles, the jockey has a decent record on him as well with one win and three places from five rides.

This will be a career best for this lad if he pulls this off tomorrow, but there is plenty in his favor. He should get a clear, uncontested lead, and Murray Dodd has ridden him to 2 wins from 5 rides on board. He responds well to good ground, and the layoff from his last run is at the right pitch for his best results. The trainer has done well here over the years, and if the horse can be turned in with two to go with enough in the tank, Greatness really could await.

Might be worth giving Robbers Bridge another chance. After a poor effort last time on heavy ground, today's surface might suit better. If he returns to his earlier form, he could certainly be involved in the finish today.

Pittsburg is bidding for a hat-trick after an emphatic win at Hereford last time. This followed on from a good win over this course and distance at the end of March. The very talented Callum Pritchard takes 5lb off his back, which is a relief given that my selection is carrying top weight. But with the weight concession and Pittsburg being in the form of his life, he has a very good chance of pulling off the hat-trick.
Royal Max can prevent the market leader's hat trick and bring up a double of their own. They won last time out and looked impressive. They still have a 7-pound advantage on the favorite.

Getaway Jewell, back from a 124-day layoff, has only been beaten by 3 lengths or less on all three starts when following a break under Brian Hughes. On a very good mark now, goes well here (2 wins) and will enjoy the quicker ground. Last run in December, ground described as good was more soft than good. Very consistent at today's trip with proper good ground. Capable of making the frame at least. 12/1 look good ew value.

The model I run simulates this race and has Jackhammer coming in first. Second biggest RPR of the field, but the second lowest OR, means Jackhammer lines up carrying the least weight of the field. Combine that with Charlie Maggs onboard claiming a further 5 lbs, and the total weight margin is 20lbs over the 2m1f distance.

Crest Of Stars showed signs of greenness in a hot Listed bumper at Cheltenham but this is a much easier ask and the better ground should help. Back from a break and likely to know more this time, he looks the one to beat if showing the promise hinted at on debut.
American Empire shaped nicely when finishing 3rd last time out. With that experience, it could win a race like this where it looks so even.

Each-way value all day here with Metaverse, whose resuming run was a midfield effort but much needed to top him off. Comes to hand quickly, as is evidenced by the fact that he has triumphed second-up previously, and off a longer break than the 190 days off before his last outing. Top rider up for an in-form trainer.

Grey Fox caused emotional scenes for his connections when winning for the Lavelle team when resuming. Course and distance winner who has shown to advantage on poly tracks previously. A repeat would be no great surprise. Has won six in this class already, thanks to an astute trainer.
The very talented James Bowen takes the reins for the good Greatrex barn here, and after a much-improved run for second last time out, this looks ready-made for them. Course and distance winner too.

Jockey D Allan rides for the good Easterby yard here on a horse who I think could be one of those that you need to catch on the right day. That was a useful effort resuming and looks set to improve on that here.
